title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 305–307 of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'). Let Γ ⊂ Autext_lac(π̂_{0,3}) be a group of outer automorphisms of the profinite free group π̂_{0,3} that respect the loop ('lacet') structure, meaning the conjugacy classes of the three inertia generators. Γ is assumed to commute with S_3, so it is a GT-hat-like group. This gives an extension M_{0,3} (also written N'_{1,1}) of Γ by Ŝ^+_{0,3}. Here Ŝ^+_{0,3} is the profinite completion of the extension of S_3 by π_{0,3}, i.e. of PSL(2,Z) = Γ(2)/±1 ⋊ S_3. Equivalently, M_{0,3} is an extension of S_3 × Γ by π̂_{0,3}.

Grothendieck has already defined:
- (36) M_{0,3} → Aut(Ŝ^+_{0,3}), inducing inner conjugation on the kernel.
- (37) GL(1,Ẑ) = Ẑ* ↪ Aut(SL(2,Ẑ)'), where SL(2,Ẑ)' = SL(2,Ẑ)/±1 is the congruence completion of PSL(2,Z).
- (38) The congruence map Ŝ^+_{0,3} = PSL(2,Z)^ → SL(2,Ẑ)'.

This page states the 'congruence condition'. The map (38) must be compatible with the outer actions of Γ:
- on Ŝ^+_{0,3}, the action is tautological, since Γ consists of S_3-commuting lacet-preserving outer automorphisms;
- on SL(2,Ẑ)', the action goes through Ẑ*/Ẑ*² and the cyclotomic character (39) χ: Γ → Ẑ*. This character is read off from the tautological outer action on π̂_{0,3}: an element acts on each inertia class by raising it to the power χ.

The congruence condition, together with (36) and (37), yields:
- (40) a well-defined homomorphism φ': M_{0,3} → GP(1,Ẑ) := PGL(2,Ẑ) = GL(2,Ẑ)/Ẑ* (outer action on the congruence quotient, realised by conjugation by GL(2,Ẑ) modulo scalars);
- (41) using χ as well, u ↦ (φ'(u), χ(u)) into PGL(2,Ẑ) × Ẑ*.

The congruence conditions say more precisely that det φ'(u) ≡ χ(u) mod Ẑ*². Hence (41) factors through (42) ψ': M_{0,3} → GL(2,Ẑ)/_2Ẑ*. This target is GL(2,Ẑ) modulo the scalars of square 1, μ_2(Ẑ) = {±1}^P. It embeds by (43) into PGL(2,Ẑ) × Ẑ* via u ↦ (ū, det u), and its image is exactly the set of pairs whose determinants agree modulo squares.

On the next page Grothendieck sets this up as a lifting problem:
- GL(2,Ẑ)/±1 → GL(2,Ẑ)/{±1}^P has kernel ν = (Z/2)^P/diag;
- pulling back gives a central extension 1 → ν → M̃_{0,3} → M_{0,3} → 1;
- he asks for a canonical splitting, i.e. a canonical homomorphism M_{0,3} → GL(2,Ẑ)/±1 that lifts ψ', expressed purely in the GT/lacet data.

In arithmetic terms, this is the combinatorial analogue of the Tate-module representation π_1(M_{1,1}/Q) → GL(2,Ẑ) (determinant = cyclotomic character), descended modulo the generic involution −1. The prime-by-prime sign ambiguity (Z/2)^P/diag is exactly what is lost by working only up to scalars.
errors: The equation label for χ: Γ → Ẑ* should be (39), not (37). (37) is already the injection GL(1,Ẑ) → Aut(SL(2,Ẑ)') on the previous page, and this page goes on to (40).
On p. 307 Grothendieck refers to 'l'hom. canonique φ' (42)'. On this page (42) is ψ' and φ' is (40), so this is a minor notational slip.

Mathematically consistent. The injectivity of (43) and the factorization criterion (det φ' ≡ χ mod squares) are correct because λ² = 1 in Ẑ* gives exactly {±1}^P. Note that SL(2,Ẑ)/±1 still has centre ν, so care is needed in identifying its automorphisms with PGL(2,Ẑ). Grothendieck only uses the image of conjugation by GL(2,Ẑ), which is fine.

ideas.what: The outer action of a GT-type group Γ on profinite PSL(2,Z) (= π̂_{0,3} ⋊ S_3, i.e. π_1 of M_{1,1} mod ±1) induces, on the congruence completion, an action through the cyclotomic character modulo squares ('condition de congruence').
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of the GT-hat / Galois action on π̂_1(M_{1,1}) with the congruence quotient SL(2,Ẑ); det of the Tate-module representation = cyclotomic character
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara; Nakamura; Lochak–Schneps (GT-hat acting on genus-1 groups); Hain–Matsumoto; Boggi (congruence topology)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and the (1,1) level qualitatively; this precise congruence condition is not stated there as far as I know.

ideas.what: Encoding the pair (outer conjugation class, cyclotomic character) as a homomorphism to GL(2,Ẑ)/μ_2(Ẑ) via the embedding into PGL(2,Ẑ) × Ẑ* by u ↦ (ū, det u).
ideas.modern_name: Projective representation with determinant data; quotient GL_2(Ẑ)/{±1}^P

ideas.what: The lifting problem to GL(2,Ẑ)/±1 as the splitting of a central extension by ν = (Z/2)^P/diag (next page). Grothendieck asks for a canonical lift defined purely from the GT/lacet data, without elliptic curves.
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial (GT-theoretic) construction of the Tate-module / Legendre-family representation; obstruction class in H²(M_{0,3}, ν)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure – arithmetically the lift comes from Tate modules of elliptic curves (Legendre family); no GT-hat-theoretic construction known to me

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up the question of a canonical homomorphism from the extension M_{0,3} (of a GT-type group Γ by PSL(2,Z)^) to GL(2,Ẑ)/±1. Such a homomorphism would lift the congruence-derived map to GL(2,Ẑ)/{±1}^P, with obstruction a central extension by (Z/2)^P/diag. For Galois groups the lift exists via the Tate module of the Legendre curve. For an abstract subgroup of GT-hat, a canonical, purely combinatorial splitting does not seem to be in the literature.
missed.quote: et les conditions congruentielles ... assurent en fait, plus précisément, que ce homom. se factorise en un homom. (42) M_{0,3} → GL(2,Ẑ)/_2Ẑ*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would give a GT-hat analogue of the 2-dimensional ℓ-adic representation attached to the universal elliptic curve. It bears on whether GT-hat 'knows' the GL_2 Tate-module structure, not just its projectivisation, and on the sign/twist ambiguities studied by Nakamura and Lochak–Schneps in genus 1.

deep.surprise_reason: The congruence compatibility through the cyclotomic character is known in substance (Ihara/Nakamura-type results). The precise formulation of the residual (Z/2)^P/diag lifting obstruction for a GT-type group, and the request for a canonical combinatorial lift to GL(2,Ẑ)/±1, is a careful unpublished detail. It is not a startling result.
transcription_corrections: 'Π' throughout → 'Γ'. The 'formé déf.' clause reads 'Γ est formé des Autext_lac(π̂_{0,3}) qui commutent à S_3'.
The label for χ: Γ → Ẑ* is (39), not (37).
'compatible à la structure : 2 cuts' → 'compatible à la structure : lacets'.
'Gl(1,Ẑ)' in (40) and (41) → 'GP(1,Ẑ)' (= PGL(2,Ẑ)), consistent with the next page.
'M^{*}_{0,3}' in (40) is just M_{0,3}; the mark is a stray/cancelled symbol.
'ce chemin' → 'ce homom.' (or similar); 'mises' probably part of 'les conditions congruentielles mises [ensemble]'.
